text:
marta: noticed a GitOps reconcile failure during the canary helm upgrade for inference-gpupool in eu-west-1, blocking the rest of the rollout
devops-bot: GitOps sync failed: helmRelease/inference-gpupool (cluster: eu-west-1) - hook pre-upgrade timed out
marta: pre-upgrade hook is our validation job that checks nodepool quotas + taints. logs show it hung on creating a test pod with gpu resource request
alex: I see: terraform apply for eu-west nodepools failed earlier with quota errors, pipeline retried but left partial nodepool object. terra-pipeline: apply failed: 1 error(s) occurred
terra-pipeline: Error: googleapi: Error 403: Quota 'CPUS_ALL_REGIONS' exceeded, quotaExceeded
ryan: so Helm pre-upgrade waits for a pod to schedule, but there are not enough GPUs because the nodepool didn't provision. helm hook hit the timeout and the release is stuck in failed hooks state
jon: can we make the hook non-blocking for canary? or fallback to a legacy model variant that doesn't require GPUs?
sre-oncall: don't want silent degradation — better to abort and rollback automatically if resources can't be provisioned. But we need a faster remediation path
marta: attempted `kubectl get helmreleases -n infra inference-gpupool -o yaml` shows hook status: 
```
status:
  lastAttemptedRevision: "3.4.0"
  conditions:
    - type: HookFailed
      message: pre-upgrade hook timed out waiting for pod: inference-preflight
```
alex: quick mitigation: remove the hook from the HelmRelease by patching the chart values to skip preflight for canary: `kubectl patch hr inference-gpupool -n infra --type merge -p '{"spec":{"values":{"preflight":{"enabled":false}}}}'`
ryan: patched, but GitOps will reverse that on next sync. We need a coordinated fix: either fix Terraform quota or create temporary spare GPU spot nodes manually in eu-west
jon: I can spin up a small spot pool and label it `gpupool-canary` to give the hook something to schedule against. Doing `gcloud container node-pools create gpupool-canary --num-nodes=1 --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-t4,count=1 --zone=europe-west1-b`
sre-oncall: hold on, spot nodes might preempt and cause flaky validation. Also cost ops flagged extra spot pools in eu-west last month. Cost concern: adding interim nodes will spike monthly committed usage if left up
alex: cost ops notified. I'll coordinate with finance for an emergency temporary allowance. For now, to unblock prod rollout, we can: 1) create a single preflight node with lower cost GPU (T4) in eu-west, 2) mark it in the TF state as ephemeral so GitOps doesn't manage it, 3) abort the failing HelmRelease then re-trigger canary once nodes are available
marta: steps I took: aborted the helmrelease reconcile via fluxctl: `flux reconcile helmrelease inference-gpupool --namespace infra --with-source` then `kubectl annotate hr inference-gpupool infra/reconcile-pause=true` to stop immediate re-sync while we provision nodes
devops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2024-498 - Helm canary blocked by nodepool quota in eu-west, assigned to eng-infra
jon: nodepool created (spot) and labeled. Preflight pod scheduled successfully. Hook job completed: logs show GPU allocation OK. Reconcile resumed
terra-pipeline: detected out-of-band nodepool; terraform plan shows drift for resource 'google_container_node_pool.gpupool' - manual nodepool not in TF state
ryan: we need to reconcile TF state after rollback: options are import the nodepool into TF state (recommended) or let GitOps remove it and reapply via TF which would cause another quota call — prefer import
alex: I'll run `terraform import module.gke.google_container_node_pool.gpupool projects/.../zones/.../nodePools/gpupool-canary` and then `terraform apply` to persist the nodepool as ephemeral but tracked. Will add a tag `redwood:ephemeral=true` and TTL in node metadata
sre-oncall: also add a circuit breaker in the Helm preflight: lower timeout + non-blocking fallback flag so future quota hiccups won't stall other uprefs
marta: agree. After import and patch, Helm canary finished: release rolled to 3.4.0 canary, metrics look good. Will follow up with a retro and a short runbook for triage (quota -> preflight stuck -> options)
jon: noted action items: add preflight timeout config, add terraform import step into emergency runbook, add alert for nodepool-provision-failure in eu-west
ryan: closing loop with cost ops: temporary nodes will be terminated in 6 hours, finance approved emergency charge
marta: thanks all :thumbsup:
